core_obligations: Dispose of the tame case: for ramification index e prime to p with separable residue extension, adjoin an e-th root of a uniformizer to get K_1, check that the integral closure A_1 is a discrete valuation ring with the expected ramification index, and conclude via Abhyankar's lemma that the quotients A_1 -> (B_1)_m are formally smooth in the m-adic topology and a fortiori weakly unramified (proof lines 35531-35543).

Assume from then on that kappa_A has characteristic p and apply the solution-after-strict-henselization lemma to reduce to the case where A and B have separably closed residue fields, verifying that the theorem's hypothesis becomes the inclusion kappa_A containing the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n} (proof lines 35546-35555).

Introduce the completions A-hat and B-hat with the displayed commutative diagram and the fraction field K-hat, and suppose given a finite M/K-hat which is a weak solution for A-hat -> B-hat and is a compositum of a separable extension with an extension obtained by adjoining a p-power root of pi (proof lines 35557-35570).

Use the approximate-separable-extension lemma to produce a finite K_1/K with K-hat tensor_K K_1 = M, and verify that A_1 -> A_1-hat is formally smooth in the m_1-hat-adic topology by propagating the formal smoothness of A -> A-hat, using that A_1 and A_1-hat are discrete valuation rings (proof lines 35571-35582).
Apply the two parts of the solutions-go-down lemma to conclude first that K_1/K is a weak solution for A -> B-hat and then for A -> B, thereby reducing to the complete case (proof lines 35583-35586).

In the complete case with separably closed residue fields of characteristic p and kappa_A containing the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, set k equal to that intersection, observe that k is algebraically closed of characteristic p, and build a Cohen ring Lambda for k (with Lambda = k[[t]] in the equicharacteristic case) together with a ring map Lambda -> A mapping t to pi (proof lines 35588-35605).
difficulty_reason: The theorem (Epp) takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L and assumes that, when kappa_A has characteristic p > 0, every element of the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n} is separable algebraic over kappa_A; it concludes the existence of a finite extension K_1/K which is a weak solution for A -> B (source lines 35517-35528). The proof first dispatches the tame case: when the ramification index e is prime to p and the residue extension is separable, adjunction of an e-th root of a uniformizer produces A_1 whose maximal-ideal quotients are formally smooth over A by Abhyankar's lemma, hence weakly unramified (proof lines 35531-35543). The interesting case is residue characteristic p, and it is handled by a two-stage reduction followed by an explicit construction. First the proof uses the strict henselization lemma to assume the residue fields separably closed, which converts the theorem's hypothesis into the inclusion kappa_A containing the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n} (proof lines 35546-35555). Then it passes to completions: it shows that a finite M/K-hat that is a weak solution for A-hat -> B-hat and is a compositum of a separable extension with an extension obtained by adjoining a p-power root of pi descends to a finite K_1/K by the approximate-separable-extension lemma, and that formal smoothness of A -> A-hat propagates to A_1 -> A_1-hat, so that the two parts of the solutions-go-down lemma apply (proof lines 35557-35586). This leaves the complete case with separably closed residue fields, where the proof introduces k as the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, observes it is algebraically closed of characteristic p, builds a Cohen ring Lambda for k and a ring map Lambda -> A sending t to pi (proof lines 35588-35605), and proceeds to construct the weak solution explicitly. The reduction ladder (strict henselization, completion, descent, formal smoothness transfer) together with the Cohen-ring construction is independent research-level content.
